pairs.why: B's stools and table throw darker, more defined cast shadows onto the grass, closer to the real card's strong ground shadows. A's shadows are softer and weaker.
A's housing turns from light to shadow in a smooth, soft gradient like the real lamp. B's hard yellow band and vents add crisper accents that the real card doesn't have.
A's rim has a soft broad sheen and a soft drop shadow on the wall behind it, as on the real clock. B sits on a floor with a flat ground shadow, which reads differently.
A's dome and drum have slightly deeper side shading and a more even soft turn. The difference is small.
A's body is a smooth navy form with a soft broad sheen, like the real housing. B's banding and vents break up the form turn.
B's rolled fabric and tubes show more form turn and a defined cast shadow, which suits the real chair's modeled look. The two are close.
A's hat has a clear light-to-shadow turn, a deep shadow under the brim, and soft sheen like the real cards. B is flatter and has a fuzzy textured look.
B has stronger form contrast, with darker shaded sides on the metal and fins and a defined highlight, like the real submarine and trumpet. A is softer and more statue-like.
